title: 3D Earth Data Visualization (Country GDP Bar Chart)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a "3D Earth + City Data Bar Chart" visualization page.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
The following importmap must be included in the HTML <head> (exactly as written), and three and OrbitControls must be imported as ES Modules inside <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
// Write your code here
</script>

[Scene and Earth]
(1) Use a sphere to represent the Earth. Use procedurally generated land outlines or a wireframe/noise texture on its surface to depict the continents (external image URL textures are prohibited).
(2) Use OrbitControls to rotate and zoom the view of the Earth.
(3) To facilitate automated validation: after the page loads, the camera must look at the center of the Earth, and the default distance between the OrbitControls camera and target point must be 15 (in the same units as the three scene); the reset camera button must restore the view to this default distance and default orientation.

[Data and Bar Chart]
(4) Hard-code data points for 20 cities in the code. Each point must include: city name, latitude lat, longitude lng, GDP value, and Population value (two scalar datasets for selection via a dropdown).
(5) Map each city to a point just outside the spherical surface, and place a THREE.CylinderGeometry (or similar) bar along the surface normal of the Earth. The bar height must be proportional to the value in the current mode (GDP or Population).
(6) Map bar colors from low to high values using a blue-to-red gradient (linear interpolation is acceptable).
(7) Use a Raycaster: when a bar is clicked, display the city name and the value for the current mode in the DOM element with id="tooltip"; when nothing is selected, it may display a placeholder or be empty, but after a selection it must be visible and its text must contain the city name.

[HUD and Controls]
(8) id="barCount": Display the number of bars.
(9) id="selectedCity": Display the name of the currently selected city (when nothing is selected, it may display "—" or be empty).
(10) id="camDistance": Display the distance from the camera to the target point (the center of the Earth); the numeric value must be consistent with the internal calculation.
(11) id="sortBy": A dropdown (select) with at least two options: "gdp" and "population" (values may be lowercase). When switched, recalculate only the bar heights and color mapping based on the other dataset; do not change the number or positions of the cities.
(12) id="resetCam": A button that, when clicked, restores the default camera and OrbitControls state (restoring the distance to 15).

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame (or promptly after each interaction), containing at least:
- barCount: number (must be 20)
- bars: Array<{ city: string, lat: number, lng: number, value: number, height: number, color: string }>, where value/height/color correspond to the current sortBy mode
- selectedCity: string (an empty string when nothing is selected)
- cameraDistance: number
- dataMode: "gdp" | "population" (must match the current value of sortBy)

Output a single HTML file that can be opened directly in a browser. All numeric values must be finite; NaN/Infinity must not occur.
